howItWorks.title: How CeyBuild Works
howItWorks.description: Getting your home services done is simple. Here's how the CeyBuild platform connects you with skilled workers from search to completion.
howItWorks.step1Desc: Browse through our categories or search for a specific service. Filter by location, ratings, and availability to find the right professional.
howItWorks.step2Desc: Review the worker's profile including their skills, experience, portfolio, ratings, and reviews from other customers.
howItWorks.step3Desc: Submit a booking request with your service requirements, preferred date, and location details.
howItWorks.step4Desc: The worker reviews your request and accepts the booking. You'll be notified when the booking is confirmed.
howItWorks.step5Desc: After the worker accepts, you'll be prompted to make an advance payment through our secure payment gateway (PayHere). This confirms your booking.
howItWorks.step6Desc: Once the advance payment is confirmed, you can communicate with the worker through the platform to finalize details.
howItWorks.step7Desc: The worker arrives at your location and performs the agreed service.
howItWorks.step8Desc: After the service is completed, you pay any remaining balance through the platform.
howItWorks.step9Desc: Share your experience by leaving a rating and review to help other customers find quality workers.
howItWorks.paymentADesc: After the worker accepts your booking, you'll be required to make an advance payment through PayHere, our integrated payment gateway. This payment secures your booking and confirms the service arrangement.
howItWorks.paymentBDesc: Your payment is verified server-side through PayHere's secure notification system. The booking status is updated only after the payment is confirmed by the gateway — never based solely on the frontend redirect.
howItWorks.paymentCDesc: After the service is completed, you'll pay any remaining balance through the platform. Once fully paid, an invoice is generated and you can leave a review.
howItWorks.paymentDDesc: All payments are processed through PayHere. CeyBuild does not store your credit card details. Transaction reference IDs are stored securely for dispute resolution and record-keeping.
howItWorks.notesVerify: Never trust payment status based only on the frontend redirect
howItWorks.notesServer: Payment is confirmed only after server-side verification
howItWorks.notesSecrets: Payment secrets are never exposed to the frontend
howItWorks.notesHandling: Failed, cancelled, and pending payments are handled separately
howItWorks.notesDuplicate: Duplicate payment processing is prevented by the system
howItWorks.notesIds: Transaction IDs are stored securely for reference
howItWorks.readyToStartDesc: Find skilled workers for your next project. It's fast, easy, and secure.

freeTools.heroDesc: Use our professional calculators to estimate materials, costs, and quantities for your home projects. Built for Sri Lankan construction standards.
freeTools.disclaimerDesc: These calculators provide estimates based on standard formulas and assumptions. Actual quantities may vary depending on paint brand, surface condition, tile layout, mix quality, and local market prices. Always consult a qualified professional for load-bearing or structural work.

paint.title: Paint Calculator
paint.desc: Calculate how much paint you need for your walls. Enter dimensions, doors, windows, and coats.
paint.heroDesc: Estimate how much paint you need for your walls
paint.wallLengthHint: Length of one wall in metres
paint.wallHeightHint: Floor to ceiling height in metres
paint.numWallsHint: How many walls of this size to paint
paint.coatsHint: Most surfaces need 2 coats for even coverage
paint.noResult: Enter your wall dimensions and click Calculate
paint.explanation: Paintable Area = (Wall Length × Height × Number of Walls) − (Doors × 1.89 m²) − (Windows × 1.44 m²). Paint Needed = Paintable Area ÷ Coverage × Coats × (1 + Wastage%).
paint.note: Note: Actual coverage varies by paint brand, surface texture, colour, and condition. Consult the paint manufacturer's data sheet for exact coverage. Dark colours and rough surfaces may require more paint.

tile.title: Tile Calculator
tile.desc: Find out how many tiles you need for your floor. Supports any tile size with wastage.
tile.heroDesc: Find out how many tiles you need for your floor
tile.floorLengthHint: Room length in centimetres (e.g. 400 cm = 4 m)
tile.piecesPerBoxHint: Check your tile box label for this number
tile.wastageHint: 10% recommended for simple layouts, 15–20% for diagonal cuts
tile.noResult: Enter your floor and tile dimensions to calculate
tile.explanation: Floor Area = Length × Width. Tile Area = Tile Length × Tile Width (converted to m²). Tiles Needed = Floor Area ÷ Tile Area. With wastage applied.
tile.note: Note: This assumes a simple grid layout. Diagonal, herringbone, or border patterns may require 15–20% wastage. Buy extra tiles for future repairs.

cement.title: Cement Calculator
cement.desc: Calculate cement and sand quantities for your mix ratio. Supports standard Sri Lankan mixes.
cement.heroDesc: Calculate cement and sand for your mortar mix
cement.volumeHint: Wet volume of mortar needed in cubic metres
cement.noResult: Enter your volume and mix ratio to calculate
cement.explanation: Dry Volume = Wet Volume × 1.33. Cement = Dry Volume × (Cement Ratio / Total Ratio) × 1440 kg/m³ ÷ Bag Size. Sand = Dry Volume × (Sand Ratio / Total Ratio) × 1.6 t/m³.
cement.note: Note: 1:4 for plastering (richer, stronger), 1:6 for brick masonry (standard), 1:3 for floor screed. Dry volume factor 1.33 accounts for shrinkage and voids. Actual yield may vary with sand moisture content and compaction.

concrete.title: Concrete Calculator
concrete.desc: Estimate cement, sand, and aggregate for your concrete pour. Choose from standard mix ratios.
concrete.heroDesc: Estimate cement, sand, and aggregate for your concrete pour
concrete.mixHint: M20 (1:1.5:3) is most common for slabs and footings
concrete.noResult: Enter your pour dimensions and select a mix grade
concrete.explanation: Wet Volume = Length × Width × Depth. Dry Volume = Wet Volume × 1.54 (factor for voids and shrinkage). For each component: Volume = Dry Volume × (Component Ratio / Total Ratio). Weight = Volume × Density.
concrete.note: This is an estimate based on nominal mix ratios. For structural or load-bearing construction, an engineer-designed concrete mix should be used. Actual quantities depend on aggregate gradation, moisture content, and compaction method. Always use quality-tested materials.

cost.title: Construction Cost Calculator
cost.desc: Estimate total project cost including materials, labour, and additional expenses. Edit unit prices.
cost.heroDesc: Estimate total project cost including materials, labour, and extras
cost.disclaimer: Estimated Cost — Not a Fixed Quotation. Prices vary by location, market conditions, and material quality in Sri Lanka. Edit unit prices to reflect your local rates.
cost.notQuote: Estimated Cost — Not a Fixed Quotation. Actual costs may vary based on location, market fluctuations, material quality, and project complexity. Always get multiple quotes from professionals.
